GenOffice Launches as an Open-Source AI Office Suite with Local Editing and CLI Support

Introduction to GenOffice

GenOffice has been introduced as a free, open-source AI-powered office suite designed for macOS, Windows, and Linux. Built under the Apache-2.0 license, the project provides native support for opening, editing, and saving standard Microsoft Office file formats including `.docx`, `.xlsx`, and `.pptx` while keeping document processing entirely local on the user's machine.

Core Applications and Features

The suite includes six primary applications alongside a tabbed shell, search utility, and AI assistant panel:

  • Docs: An editor for `.docx` files featuring integrated AI review capabilities and tracked changes.
  • Sheets: A spreadsheet application utilizing live formulas and charts rather than static pasted values, backed by a Rust-based processing sidecar.
  • Slides: A presentation tool that generates `.pptx` decks from prompts, featuring slide-by-slide narration recording.
  • PDF: Provides in-place text editing and on-device PDF-to-Word conversion using local layout analysis.
  • HTML & Markdown: Dedicated block and source editors supporting local exports, linked notes, and graph views.

Local-First AI Integration

Unlike traditional cloud-bound assistants, GenOffice embeds an AI agent directly into the document workflow rather than confining it to a side chat box. Edits are applied as tracked changes with one-click rollbacks.

  • Privacy and Key Management: Users can either sign in via Genspark for routed proxy access or bring their own API keys for providers such as Anthropic Claude, OpenAI, Gemini, DeepSeek, and local model servers.
  • Smart Search: A local SQLite full-text index powers document searches across folders, with optional reranking available via the TypeSafe Jev judgment model.
  • Ask AI: Starred documents can function as a local knowledge base, providing answers with explicit citations linked directly to the source files.

Developer and Agent Tooling

GenOffice provides advanced scripting and agent interfaces via a bundled command-line tool (`genoffice`) and Model Context Protocol (MCP) support.

  • Coding Agent Integration: Compatible AI coding assistants—including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and GitHub Copilot—can utilize the provided skills to create, inspect, and modify real Office files locally without requiring a graphical window.
  • Cross-Platform Availability: Installers are distributed for macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel), Windows (x64 and Arm), and Linux via `.deb`, `.rpm`, and AppImage formats.

Verification and Availability

The source code and release builds are publicly hosted on GitHub. Users can verify technical requirements, installation steps, and third-party dependency notices directly through the official repository.
